l3_description: Creates a new empty raster dataset with specified properties.
Adds a new field (column) to a table or feature class with specified data type and properties.
Deletes one or more fields from a table or feature class.
Modifies field properties such as name alias or data type.
Calculates field values using an expression or formula.
Merges multiple datasets into a new single dataset.
Returns the number of features or records in a dataset.
Converts the data type of raster pixels (e.g., from float to integer, or 32-bit to 8-bit). This is also known as casting.
Creates buffer polygons around input features at a specified distance.
Computes geometric intersection of input features retaining only overlapping areas with attributes from all inputs.
Combines all features from multiple input layers preserving all geometries and attributes.
Removes portions of input features that overlap with erase features.
Extracts features that do not overlap between two input layers (inverse of Intersect).
Extracts input features that fall within the clip features extent like a cookie cutter.
Updates input features by replacing overlapping areas with update features; non-overlapping input areas preserved.
Aggregates geometries into multi-geometry features (MultiPoint/MultiLineString/MultiPolygon) based on attribute.
Joins attributes from one feature layer to another based on spatial relationship (intersects/contains/within/touches/etc.) without modifying geometry.
Splits line features at locations where they intersect point features.
Converts features to point features at specified locations (centroid/inside/start/end/mid/vertices).
Creates minimum enclosing geometry (rectangle/circle/convex hull/envelope) for features.
Selects features or table records based on attribute query (SQL expression).
Extracts features to new dataset based on attribute query.
Extracts features to new dataset based on spatial relationship with other features.
Filters features based on geometry properties (area/length/vertex count/perimeter).
Separates multipart features into individual singlepart features or component geometries.
Clips a raster dataset using vector polygon boundaries; pixels outside the geometry are set to NoData.
Clips a raster dataset using a rectangular bounding box (extent); retains all pixels within the extent.
Extracts raster cells that satisfy a specified condition (attribute-based query or value range).
Selects specific bands from a multi-band raster dataset.
Updates the raster mask based on a condition; sets invalid pixels to NoData.
Adds or concatenates bands from multiple images into a single multi-band image.
Calculates statistics for raster values within zones defined by vector polygons.
Calculates statistics for each pixel based on values in a defined neighborhood (moving window).
Computes summary statistics for the entire raster dataset (or within analysis extent).
[L3_03_03_01] Performs basic arithmetic operations (addition | [L3_03_03_04] Applies advanced mathematical functions (exponential | [L3_03_03_06] Performs binary bitwise operations (AND
[L3_03_03_02] Performs Boolean logical operations (AND | [L3_03_03_03] Performs relational comparison operations between rasters or raster and scalar values.
Remaps raster values based on a lookup table; transforms old values to new values or class codes.
Divides continuous raster values into discrete classes using equal interval
Reclassifies raster based on conditional expression; assigns specified values where condition is true or false.
Transforms raster to a different coordinate reference system; may also change resolution during transformation.
Merges multiple rasters into a single continuous raster using rule-based pixel selection (first/last/min/max/mean).
Calculates vegetation indices such as NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) and EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) using multi-spectral bands.
Calculates domain-specific spectral indices: NDWI for water
Converts sensor Digital Numbers (DN) to at-sensor radiance or Top-of-Atmosphere (TOA) reflectance using calibration coefficients.
Corrects for atmospheric scattering and absorption to derive surface reflectance from TOA reflectance.
Converts thermal infrared band DN or radiance to brightness temperature in Kelvin or Celsius.
Identifies cloud and cloud shadow pixels using spectral characteristics and geometric projection.
Transforms multi-spectral data using PCA (Principal Component Analysis) or Tasseled Cap to create uncorrelated or physically meaningful components.
Fuses high-resolution panchromatic band with lower-resolution multispectral bands to create enhanced spatial resolution color imagery.
Parses quality/QA bands using bitwise operations to extract quality flags and filter low-quality pixels.
Filters an image collection by start and end dates to select images within a specific temporal window.
Filters an image collection by specific months or seasons (e.g., summer months 6-8) across multiple years.
Filters images by day of year (DOY, 1-365/366) to select specific periods regardless of year.
Filters an image collection based on metadata properties such as cloud cover, satellite orbit, or quality flags.
Filters an image collection to include only images that intersect with a specified geographic region.
Limits the number of images in a collection by taking the first N images or applying count constraints.

[L3_03_10_01] Computes the pixel-wise median across all images in a time series, reducing outliers and noise. | [L3_03_10_02] Computes the pixel-wise arithmetic mean across all images in a time series. | [L3_03_10_03] Computes the pixel-wise maximum value across all images in a time series. | [L3_03_10_04] Computes the pixel-wise minimum value across all images in a time series. | [L3_03_10_05] Computes the pixel-wise sum of all images in a time series. | [L3_03_10_08] Computes pixel-wise percentiles (e.g., 25th, 75th) across all images in a time series for robust statistical aggregation. | [L3_03_10_09] Counts the number of valid (non-masked) observations per pixel across a time series. | [L3_03_10_10] Selects the first or last image in a temporally sorted image collection. | [L3_03_10_12] Aggregates images within regular time intervals (daily, monthly, yearly) using a reduction function.
Fits a polynomial regression model to time series data to identify non-linear temporal trends.
Detects changes by subtracting pixel values between two images from different dates.
Calculates the duration of the growing season from time series vegetation indices.
Calculates slope gradient (rate of change in elevation) in degrees or percent from a DEM.
Calculates the downslope direction (compass bearing) of maximum rate of elevation change.
Generates shaded relief map simulating illumination from a specified sun position for visualization.
Automatically determines optimal number of groups and assigns features to groups using spatial and attribute characteristics.
Applies a single symbol style (color size shape) to all features in a layer.
Combines multiple raster bands into RGB color image for true-color or false-color visualization.
Adds text labels to map features based on attribute values with placement and styling options.
Exports vector features to Shapefile format for data sharing and archiving.
Exports raster data to GeoTIFF format with georeferencing.
Exports raster to non-georeferenced image format (PNG JPEG) for display.
Extracts labeled training samples from imagery or time-series stacks by intersecting ROI features with pixel values, writing spectral profiles and class IDs to a sample table.
Builds balanced samples per class or per stratum by randomly generating points/pixels within training polygons, enforcing quotas or proportional weights.
Computes vegetation, water, burn, or soil indices (NDVI, NDWI, NBR, SAVI, etc.) from multispectral imagery to enrich feature stacks.
Generates GLCM textures, entropy, variance, or contextual statistics in moving windows to characterize spatial patterns.
Applies opening/closing, top-hat/bottom-hat, or multi-scale morphological filters to emphasize shapes and objects in imagery.
Aggregates time-series imagery into metrics such as temporal mean, median, max NDVI, amplitude, or phenological phases.
Transforms correlated bands/features into orthogonal components (PCA, MNF) or embeds them using autoencoders to reduce redundancy.
Fits an ensemble of decision trees for categorical prediction using user-defined tree counts, depth, and sampling strategy.
Optimizes an SVM classifier/regressor with kernel selection, penalty, and gamma parameters for high-dimensional feature spaces.
Applies a trained classifier to imagery/feature stacks to produce labeled rasters or vectors representing thematic classes.
Generates per-class probability rasters, confidence layers, or uncertainty scores to quantify prediction strength.

[L3_08_05_01] Clusters pixels/features into K groups using Euclidean distance in feature space to derive unsupervised land-cover classes. | [L3_08_05_02] Runs ISODATA/EM-style clustering allowing automatic split/merge of classes based on variance and distance thresholds. | [L3_08_05_03] Generates object segments (superpixels) using algorithms like SNIC or SLIC to support OBIA workflows and contextual features.

Computes confusion matrix from classification results and reference data, calculating overall accuracy, producer's/consumer's accuracy, kappa coefficient, F-score, and other classification accuracy metrics.
Applies simple kernels (mean, median, bilateral) to reduce salt-and-pepper noise while preserving edges.
Refines cloud and shadow masks using spectral tests, morphological dilation, or multi-spectral indexes.
Performs global or reference-based histogram equalization/matching to enhance contrast.
Applies gamma, log, or power-law tone curves for brightness adjustments and dynamic range compression.
Matches color/illumination between scenes by transferring histograms or tone curves.
Uses Laplacian or directional gradients to emphasize edges and micro-texture.
Selects the best pixel from a time series based on quality criteria (cloud-free highest NDVI etc) to create a composite.
Averages or takes the median of time-series observations to reduce noise and create stable composites.
Combines co-registered images using pixel-wise weighted averaging based on quality variance or user-defined weights.
Concatenates feature bands from multiple sources (spectral indices textures derivatives) into a single multi-band stack.
Aligns one image to another using geometric transformation based on control points or optimization.
Checks feature geometry for validity and identifies errors.
Converts vector data between different GIS vector formats (Shapefile to GeoJSON to Geodatabase to GeoPackage etc.).
Extends line features to a specified distance or to intersect other features.
Extracts or generates point samples from input features at specified locations or random/regular distribution.
Repairs invalid feature geometries automatically.
Converts between raster and vector formats: raster to polygon/point/line or vector to raster.
Transforms spatial data from one coordinate reference system (CRS) to another including projection and datum transformation.
